title: POC Weekly Caching Sync
summary: Weekly POC sync to review caching pilot metrics (prefix vs KV hit rates), tune TTLs and prompt reuse, and align on next benchmark run and artifacts to share. SE presented hit-rate improvements after template consolidation; customer asked about eviction/retry behavior and private deployment implications.
next_steps: Redwood to share updated caching config + benchmark spreadsheet
Catalyst to provide 2 weeks of production sample queries and sample session IDs
Run 48-hour bench with 50k queries and report p95/p99 latencies
Schedule security call if Catalyst wants Private deployment evaluation
action_items: Liam Chen - export latest cache hit-rate dashboard + explanation of cache key strategy (due 2026-10-16)
Sara Gomez - share sample query traces and session-id schema (due 2026-10-18)
Maya Patel - send pricing for Dedicated pilot and link to SOC2/ISO docs (due 2026-10-15)
Priya Menon - confirm network constraints for VPC testing (due 2026-10-20)
Alex Rivera - add instrumentation for TTL misses counts to their observability (due 2026-10-21)
transcript:
Header: 2026-10-13 10:00 PT | Duration: ~45m | Attendees: Maya, Liam, Jordan (Redwood) / Sara, Ethan, Priya, Alex (Catalyst)

0:00 Speaker 1: okay... hey everyone thanks for joining the weekly caching sync, we had a couple of agenda items, quick results from last week's benchmark and then tuning suggestions. maya?, mm
0:18 Maya Patel: yep uh hi all, thanks for the time. quick call out: we ran the longer prefix consolidation test and saw overall KV cache hit rate move from ~18% to ~42% for the conversational flows you shared. not perfect but big lift.
0:36 Liam Chen: to add, those numbers are for a 2-hour synthetic run with your session id distribution and 2k distinct prompts; real traffic will vary but the trend holds.
:50 Sara Gomez: wait 18 to 42, that's great — what's driving it, is it just template hashing?
1:05 Liam Chen: mostly prompt dedup + canonicalization. we collapsed similar templates, normalized slot ordering and applied a prefix match window so the KV key is more likely to hit. also trimmed some metadata that was previously in the key.
1:24 Ethan Park: when you say prefix match window, is that the same as the prefix cache you mentioned in the doc? i saw both prefix and kv in the sheet and was a little confused.
1:38 Liam Chen: yeah sorry maybe overload of terms — we use prefix cache to store deterministic prompt beginnings (the system and opening user turns) and KV cache for full input->kv mapping on the last tokens. prefix helps with reuse across sessions, KV captures exact-match contexts.
1:58 Priya Menon: ok sounds good; how are evictions handled? i remember last time we saw spikes where cache got flushed and latency jumped.
2:12 Jordan Reyes: good question; eviction is LRU-ish with size and TTL. the synthetic run used a 30m TTL; you saw spikes because of a purge triggered by a torus rollout in the cluster — that was unrelated to TTL.
2:28 Sara Gomez: oh that rollout — right. for our prod traffic, we have many short sessions and a lot of very similar prompts, so TTL tuning seemed important. what do you recommend?
2:41 Liam Chen: for your distro i'd recommend a shorter TTL for KV entries (5-10m) and longer TTL for prefix items (2-6 hours). prefix entries are fewer and have higher reuse across users.
2:57 Ethan Park: hmm 2-6 hours feels long, will that blow up memory?
3:05 Liam Chen: it depends on cardinality — since prefixes dedupe heavily, you get a lot of reuse per cached item; memory grows less than linear. we can show you projected memory curves with your sample traces.
3:19 Alex Rivera: i'll take the sample traces, alex here — what format do you want? jsonl with session_id?
3:26 Maya Patel: jsonl is perfect. include session_id, timestamp, prompt, and a label if possible. pti
3:34 Sara Gomez: noted — we'll sanitize PII before sharing.
3:40 Speaker 2 (transcription glitch): uh yeah okay next — can you walk through the call path when there's a cache miss? i want to understand retry logic and how we degrade.
3:52 Liam Chen: sure. on miss we always fall back to model call to the selected variant, we attempt best-effort KV prefetch for likely next-turns, and if the latency SLO is tight we fall back to a smaller quantized model. the important bit is we don't block on prefetch; prefetch is async.
4:12 Priya Menon: async prefetch ok, but do we have a circuit-breaker so prefetch storms don't cascade on the model infra?
4:21 Liam Chen: yes there's a token budget per instance and backpressure to the routing layer, plus rate limits per customer. we can tune those.
4:30 Ethan Park: this ties into our cost concern — more prefetching = more tokens = cost. what tradeoffs are you seeing?
4:40 Liam Chen: right — prefetch increases calls but reduces repeated generation for short sessions. our recommendation: conservative prefetch (e.g., prefetch next 1 turn) with adaptive scale based on observed hit-rate. that'll give most of the benefit without linear cost.
4:58 Maya Patel: speed vs cost tradeoff is classic. also our Optimize module suggested quantization on tails of traffic to reduce token cost.
5:08 Sara Gomez: quick question — you mentioned canonicalizing slot ordering earlier; will that affect any business logic? we have prompts that rely on ordering for slot interpretation.
5:22 Liam Chen: good catch. canonicalization should be applied only to fields that are order-invariant. we can add guarding so we don't canonicalize order-sensitive slots. we'll send the exact rules we applied in the test.
5:35 Jordan Reyes: that'll be in the config doc + a diff of the template changes. link will be shared in the notes.
5:42 Ethan Park: do you have numbers for p95/p99 latency with and without cache from the run?
5:50 Liam Chen: yes: baseline (no cache) p95 ~520ms p99 ~980ms; with current KV+prefix settings p95 dropped to ~210ms p99 ~420ms in the synthetic run. again depends on tail distribution in your real traffic.
6:12 Sara Gomez: that's promising. what's the hit-rate by flow? some flows we care more about (search, checkout).
6:22 Liam Chen: yep. search flow hit-rate ~62% after template consolidation; checkout intent flow lower ~28% because it's more unique per session.
6:33 Priya Menon: for checkout we probably can't rely on caching as much; maybe focus on batching or model selection fallback.
6:42 Maya Patel: agree, caching is complementary — dedicated capacity and quantization on database-intensive paths helps.
6:50 Ethan Park: can you remind us of the KV key composition? i want to be sure there's no PII in keys.
6:58 Liam Chen: KV key is hashed over system prompt id + canonicalized user prompt (sanitized) + template id. we never include raw user identifiers in the key. hashing applied at edge.
7:15 Sara Gomez: good. also about cache warmup for daily spikes — any suggestions?
7:23 Liam Chen: two options: offline preload with top-N prefixes or warmup traffic via a small synthetic runner pre-peak. both workable. for you, top-N prefix preload looks simplest.
7:34 Alex Rivera: top-N prefix mode — how do we compute N? is it dynamic?
7:40 Liam Chen: we recommend starting with top 5k prefixes from last 7 days and then adjust; we can include a script.
7:48 Maya Patel: quick status check on integration tasks from last week — Alex were you able to add the session_id in traces?
7:55 Alex Rivera: partially, we have session_id in 70% of traces; working on retroactive stitching for older logs.
8:03 Sara Gomez: ok that's OK, we'll prioritize new logs being full.
8:08 Ethan Park: can we talk about prefix expiration policy — do you prefer LRU vs TTL for prefix cache?
8:14 Liam Chen: TTL + adaptive eviction gives best control. LRU alone can evict hot prefixes during bursty periods. TTL keeps highly reused prefixes around.
8:24 Priya Menon: can Redwood support both at once?
8:28 Jordan Reyes: yes — TTL per item with LRU as a secondary eviction works well. we'll share config sample.
8:36 Maya Patel: cool. any security concerns remaining? Priya?
8:40 Priya Menon: we want to see audit logs for cache hits/misses and KMS usage. also need confirmation keys are rotated and never leave customer VPC in Private.
8:53 Maya Patel: we'll share SOC2 + ISO docs and the Private deployment KMS design. for hosted we log hits/misses metadata but not payloads; for Private everything is customer-controlled.
9:07 Sara Gomez: thanks. can you put those docs in the shared folder?
9:10 Maya Patel: yes i'll add links after the call — redwood.com/confidential/soc2 (note: placeholder) and drive link to the benchmark sheet.
9:22 Ethan Park: last technical question — you mentioned adaptive prefetch — is that model-aware (i.e., different for quantized vs full)?
9:30 Liam Chen: yes we can tune prefetch aggressiveness by route and target model size, preferring smaller prefetch budgets for quantized variants.
9:40 Sara Gomez: great. I think we should run the 48-hour bench with our real sample traces next, is that doable?
9:47 Maya Patel: yes we'll coordinate — our ask is sanitized sample traces by Friday. we'll kick off bench early next week.
9:55 Jordan Reyes: next actions: upload config, scheduler for bench, and the security docs.
10:03 Speaker 3: thanks everyone. recap?
10:08 Maya Patel: recap: 1) Catalyst sends sanitized traces (Sara/Alex) 2) Redwood runs 48h bench with updated KV+prefix settings and TTL recommendations 3) Redwood shares memory projection and cost delta 4) share SOC2/Private KMS docs. we'll meet same time next week to review results.
10:26 Ethan Park: perfect, thanks.
10:30 Sara Gomez: thanks all, bye.
10:33 End of call

Notes: transcription has occasional label glitches; timestamps approximate. Shared artifacts: https://drive.redwood/example/poc-caching-bench.xlsx , SOC2 link placeholder: https://redwood.example/soc2-docs
questions: What's the recommended TTL split between prefix and KV for Catalyst's distribution?
How to avoid canonicalization breaking order-sensitive prompts?
Can Redwood provide sample memory projection with Catalyst's cardinality?
